    Finds the widest add spacing so that, at the stress point (last add + N spacings further), the loss incl. spread/commission stays within budget and the margin level stays above the stop-out level, using this broker's margin and cost settings. Funding is excluded here — keep a buffer for it. With a fixed budget, more adds means less distance covered (each add increases the loss per point); adds bring the breakeven closer instead.

    One simulated trade starts at the first bar of every trading day in the range. Each trade runs bar by bar (H4; daily bars before 2016 for gold/WTI): open gaps first, then the adverse extreme (adds, stops, worst drawdown), then the favourable extreme (target). In a bar where an add fills, only the close may reach the new target. Spread + commission are charged per contract; funding/swap at every server-day rollover (calendar nights, so weekends count as the triple). Money in your display currency (Calculator tab).

    Read this before trusting the numbers
    
  
    This is past history, not a forecast: the DAX roughly quadrupled since 2012 and gold rose ~15× since 2000, so a buy-and-add plan looks great and a sell-and-add plan looks terrible largely because of that trend. Starts on consecutive days overlap heavily (a single bad month shows up as dozens of "trades"), so the cases are not independent and the percentages overstate how much evidence there is. "Still open" trades are marked at the last price, and the worst ones may never recover. Prices are Pepperstone cash/spot CFDs (DAX before 2020 from HistData); Plus500 quotes futures-based prices that differ by the carry (DAX ~30–140 pts higher, oil by the curve), and their funding is estimated. Spreads are fixed preset values (real spreads widen in fast markets and at the open), swaps use today's preset rates for the whole history (real rates changed with interest rates), and slippage and margin calls are not modelled — a real broker would stop you out if equity ran out.

    Ranges
    
  
    
  
    Position % = where the price sits inside each range (0% = low, 100% = high). Yellow = price, blue = your entries (▸/◂ when outside the range). Days are broker-server days (NY+7, one trading session per date); weeks start Monday. Highs/lows from embedded H4 bars. Refresh the embedded data with tools/simbuild/refresh_data.sh.
